key_insight: In epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, terahertz and Hall measurements give matching mobilities, indicating truly intrinsic charge transport across macroscopic length scales.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical benchmark for defect-free perovskite transport and a methodology for validating mobility in emerging semiconductor devices.
method: Concurrent Hall-effect and optical pump-terahertz probe (OPTP) measurements on the same single-crystal sample
Epitaxial CsPbBr3 single-crystal device platform to compare local and macroscopic transport
Temperature-dependent mobility analysis to test for band-like intrinsic behavior
evidence_signal: Both techniques reported consistent room-temperature hole mobilities of about 30 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and similar power-law temperature exponents.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated on high-quality epitaxial single crystals, so it may not directly translate to more defect-rich thin films or polycrystalline devices.
paper_title: Matching Terahertz and Hall Mobilities as a Hallmark of Intrinsic Charge Transport in Metal-Halide Perovskites
